title: Is That Health App Really Safe? IEEE Is Checking for You!
summary: There are over 55,000 medical apps out there that say they can help you feel better. But here’s the scary part: most of them have never been tested by anyone to make sure they actually work or keep your info safe. That means an app for depression or chronic pain might not help at all—or could even be risky. To fix this, the IEEE Standards Association created a new program. It’s called the IEEE Global Medical Mobile App Assessment and Registry. Think of it like a seal of approval. Experts check each app for things like: Does it really help patients? Is it designed fairly? Does it protect your private health data? Only apps that pass get listed in a public directory. Yuri Quintana, who leads the program, says many apps just have good marketing, not good science. Some companies even trick people by saying all their apps are certified when only one is. The registry is voluntary, so not every app will be in it. But if you see an app with the IEEE check, you’ll know it’s been looked at by a team of doctors, tech experts, and patient advocates. That’s a big step toward making digital health safer for everyone!
why_it_matters: Just like you wouldn’t eat food without checking if it’s safe, this registry helps you know which health apps you can trust, making it easier to take care of yourself and your family.

background_read: The IEEE (the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers) is a worldwide group that creates rules for how technology should work, from Wi-Fi to medical devices.
Because many health apps don’t have to be tested by the government before they are sold, groups like the IEEE step in to give people trustworthy information.
Yuri Quintana (the program’s leader) warns that many apps rely on flashy advertising, not real science, and some companies even pretend all their apps are certified when only one is.
Article_Structure: WHO: IEEE Standards Association, Yuri Quintana
WHAT: launched a voluntary assessment and registry that gives medical apps a seal of approval after expert review
WHERE: global, with experts checking apps from around the world
WHY: because most health apps are never tested, can be useless or risky, and the program helps people find ones that actually work and protect data

perspectives.description: They appreciate having a trusted list of apps that have been examined by real experts, so they can make safer choices.
Some companies think the testing takes too long and costs too much, so they might not join, leaving many apps still unchecked.
They see this as a good start but worry that a voluntary program is not enough; they think stronger rules may be needed to protect everyone.
